title: Woman Killed By Suspected Stray Bullet in Moyale Amid Ethiopia Conflict
summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- A 65-year-old woman has been killed in Moyale after she was struck on the head by an object believed to be a stray bullet amid ongoing clashes between two regions in neighbouring Ethiopia.

title: All of Africa Today - November 3, 2026
summary: [allAfrica]

title: Contested Land, Historical Grievances - Tracing Borana Pastoralists' Territorial Loss and Roots of Moyale Conflict
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- In his 2001 study, "Participation and Governance in the Development of Borana: Southern Ethiopia," researcher Johan Helland noted that, historically, Borana territory extended well beyond present-day Ethiopia into areas of what are now Kenya and Somalia, reaching as far as the Tana and Juba rivers. This history points out that Borana Oromoo have a broad geographical territory and the importance of land for pastoral communities.

title: Survivors Flee Hayiq Jari IDP Camp After Deadly Drone Strike
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Displaced people are fleeing the Hayiq Jari 2 Turkey camp for internally displaced persons (IDP) in Amhara region following a deadly drone strike that killed at least 18 civilians and injured 22 others, with survivors reporting the closure of essential support services and growing uncertainty over where they can go.

title: Somaliland Officials Condemn Attacks On Oromo Residents in Borama After More Than 150 Homes Reportedly Damaged
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Somaliland officials and community leaders have condemned attacks targeting Oromo residents in Borama, where more than 150 homes belonging to the residents were reportedly damaged or looted, as authorities announced arrests and pledged legal action.

title: Sudan Says 70 Drone Attacks Launched From Ethiopia Killed, Wounded Hundreds Over Eight Months
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Sudan has accused Ethiopia of enabling drone attacks launched from its territory that killed or wounded hundreds of civilians and soldiers, saying it documented 70 attacks involving 187 one-way attack drones between 15 February and 27 October, according to a report by the army-led Transitional Sovereignty Council.

title: Oromia Says 73 Detained Over Arsi Killings As Residents Report Post-Attack Arrests
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- The Oromia Regional Government says 73 individuals have been taken into custody in connection with deadly attacks in Shirka Woreda, Southeast Oromia, describing the arrests as part of security operations against what it calls "Tsimdo" and other armed groups, amid earlier reports of mass detentions of residents following the killings.

title: Authority Suspends Registration of Ethiopia's Oldest Independent Newspaper Indefinitely
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- The Ethiopian Media Authority (EMA) has indefinitely suspended the registration certificate of Media and Communication Center PLC, publisher of the Amharic Reporter and English-language The Reporter newspapers, citing alleged repeated violations of the law and professional ethics.

title: Will Renewed Conflict Derail Ethiopia's Economic Growth?
summary: [DW] Ethiopia's economy is growing strongly. But renewed fighting in the north of the BRICS member state could deter investment, strain public finances and push up the cost of living.

title: Govt Relocates Two KCSE Centres in Moyale Over Kenya-Ethiopia Border Clashes
summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- The Ministry of Education has relocated two national examination centres in Moyale Sub-County, Marsabit County, following insecurity triggered by clan clashes along the Kenya-Ethiopia border.

title: Emirates Businesswomen Council Sees Growing Investment Opportunities in Ethiopia
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Chairperson of the Emirates Businesswomen Council Aisha Mohammed Saeed Al Mulla has praised Ethiopia's growing business potential.

title: Geopolitical Rivalries, Economic Pressures and Climate Risks Dominate the Global Agenda
summary: [ENA] The final week of October 2026 underscored the increasingly interconnected nature of global affairs, as geopolitical rivalries, diplomatic efforts to contain conflicts, economic uncertainty and escalating climate risks continued to shape the international agenda.

title: Ethiopia Calls for Fairer Global Representation As Al Jazeera Marks 30 Years of Broadcasting
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia has reaffirmed its openness to Al Jazeera and other international media organizations, emphasizing its commitment to facilitating responsible journalism grounded in fairness, balance and accuracy.

title: Ethiopia Steps Up Preparations for Major African Health Conference
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia has entered the final stages of preparations to host the fifth Conference on Public Health in Africa (CPHIA 2026) in Addis Ababa from November 23 to 27, Health Minister Mekdes Daba said.

title: Violence in the North Is Pushing Health System to the Brink, WHO Chief Warns
summary: [UN News] The head of the World Health Organization (WHO) called on Monday for greater protection for civilians caught in conflict in northern Ethiopia following deadly drone strikes this past weekend.

title: Sudan Govt Accuses Ethiopia of Backing RSF Drone Attacks, Analysts Question UN Complaint
summary: [Dabanga] Khartoum / Addis Ababa -- Sudan's government has accused Ethiopia of allowing the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) to use its territory to launch drone attacks against civilian infrastructure, filing formal complaints with the United Nations Security Council and the African Union's Peace and Security Council.

title: Ethiopia's Defence Modernization Signals New Era of Strategic Deterrence
summary: [ENA] Ethiopia's announcement of the acquisition of advanced Russian-made Su-35 fighter jets and plans to receive S-400 air defence systems marks a significant development in the country's efforts to modernize its national defence capabilities, strengthen the protection of its airspace and reinforce its strategic deterrence.

title: Danish Diplomat Hails Ethiopia's Energy Advances As Catalyst for Strategic Partnership
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia's growing renewable energy capacity and ambitious green development agenda are creating significant opportunities to deepen strategic cooperation with Denmark in clean energy, water management and climate resilience, a Danish diplomat has told ENA.

title: Israeli Water Expert Sees Ethiopia's Water Potential As Catalyst for Agricultural Superpower Ambition
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia has enormous potential to advance agriculture and other development sectors through additional dams and other water-related projects, an Israeli water-technology expert said.

title: Council of Ministers Condemns Attacks On Service Facilities By Drones Launched From Ethiopia
summary: [SNA] Khartoum (SUNA) - The Council of Ministers held its regular meeting in Khartoum on Sunday, chaired by Prime Minister Dr Kamil Idris.

title: PM Abiy's Medemer Govt Senior Leadership Taking 'Military Training'at Hurso Center
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Senior leaders of Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's Medemer Government are undergoing military training at the Hurso Military Training Center, according to PM Abiy, who said the exercise as part of efforts to strengthen leadership capacity, discipline, national security, and the implementation of its broader development vision.

title: Diplomatic Visibility, Strategic Deterrence and Growing Stakes in the Red Sea Region
summary: [ENA] The final week of October 2026 brought Ethiopia into sharper international focus, as the country advanced its defence modernization, strengthened strategic partnerships and renewed attention to its interests in the Abay (Nile) Basin and Red Sea region.

title: Abiy Joins Ministers in Military Drills, Calls for Disciplined Leadership
summary: [Horn Diplomat] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has joined ministers and senior government officials in military training, saying discipline and preparedness could strengthen civilian leadership and help deliver the government's development goals.

title: U.S. Customs Releases Ethiopia-Made Solar Cell Shipments After Supply Chain Review
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) has released shipments of solar cells manufactured at a Japanese company's facility in Ethiopia following a review of its supply chain documentation, SolarQuarter reported.

title: 'Ethiopia's Return to a Sea Port Is Inevitable': Navy Commander Calls for Regional Maritime Cooperation
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Ethiopian Navy Commander Vice Admiral Kindu Gezu has called for closer regional cooperation and dialogue on maritime security, saying Ethiopia's return to a seaport is inevitable and requires stronger engagement with neighboring countries.

title: Fading Hopes, Rising Needs - Renewed Fighting Threatens Another Humanitarian Catastrophe in Tigray
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Renewed fighting in Tigray, northern Ethiopia, is pushing an already vulnerable population towards another humanitarian catastrophe. Nearly four years after the November 2022 Pretoria peace agreement was signed to end the devastating war between the Ethiopian federal government and Tigrayan forces, renewed hostilities have raised serious concerns about civilian safety, mass displacement, food insecurity, and the disruption of essential services.

title: As Tens of Thousands Flee Ethiopia to Kenya, UN Agency Warns of Growing Humanitarian Needs
summary: [allAfrica] Geneva -- The UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR) says humanitarian needs are growing in an unfolding crisis on the Kenya-Ethiopia border as ongoing clashes on the Ethiopian side have forced tens of thousands of people to cross into Kenya in search of safety.

title: Youth Leadership in Africa: Four Young Leaders on Opportunity, Inclusion, and Change
summary: [Mastercard Foundation] Too often, young people are invited to share experiences after decisions have already been made. Yet our experiences are evidence of what works, what does not, and what systems need to change. Listening matters, but it is only the beginning. What truly matters is whether our perspectives shape priorities, inform decisions, direct resources, and strengthen accountability.
